newsitem.title: USA: Southern Peru decision at least 4 yrs away.
newsitem.headline: Southern Peru decision at least 4 yrs away.

text.p: Southern Peru Copper Corp will not be making a decision on Stage III of its expansion and modernization project before 2001, chief executive Charles Preble said Thursday.
Speaking to reporters after the annual meeting, he said the decision will come "not before 2001."
Stages I and II, which call for spending of $1 billion, are on schedule, he said.
As reported earlier, work on Phase I began after the company received commitments for $600 million of financing during the first quarter.

This expansion of Southern Peru's Cuajone Mine, scheduled for completion in early 1999, is expected expand copper production 130 million pounds per year, or 19 percent, at a cost of $245 million. Engineering is underway on Stage II, the $787 million, two phase Ilo Smelter modernization to be completed in 2001 and 2003.
Preble told the annual meeting Stage III will involve a $750 million expansion of of the Cuajone Mine and the Ilo Smelter expected to boost copper production 30 percent.

He also said each $0.01 per pound change in the average price of copper results in a $0.052 per share change in Southern Peru's annual earnings, while each $1 per ounce change in silver prices results in a $0.022 earnings change and each $1 per pound change in molybdenum prices moves earnings per share $0.044 per share.

In the first quarter, the company's average copper price, based on prices on the London Metal Exchange, was $1.10, down from $1.17 a year earlier. Silver averaged $5.01 per ounce compared to $5.54 in 1996's first quarter and molybdenum was $4.38 per pound compared to $3.97.
Last week the company reported first quarter earnings per share of $0.70, up from $0.61 in 1996's initial three months.
